runs.description: These datasets were generated by a 5-step agentic analysis pipeline for an AMCIS 2026 IS research paper titled "Strategic AI Orientation Enabled by Trust & Integration Readiness." The pipeline uses GPT-4.1 to systematically analyse 34 literature sources (peer-reviewed articles, governance standards like NIST AI RMF / EU AI Act / ISO 42001, and practitioner reports from McKinsey / Deloitte / BCG) plus MITRE ATLAS adversarial ML case studies. Step 2 performs a crosswalk mapping 42 governance requirements (from NIST AI RMF, NIST GenAI Profile, EU AI Act, and OWASP Top 10 LLM) to 18 architecture controls, producing competency statements classified into two bundles: "Trust Readiness" (governance/policy/risk) and "Integration Readiness" (architecture/engineering). Step 3 codes 52 real-world MITRE ATLAS AI security incidents by harm type, failure mode, and implied competency gap, then maps them to 16 sub-competencies to validate framework coverage. Known gaps: 4 sub-competencies (TR-5 Regulatory Compliance, TR-7 Human Override, IR-5 GenAIOps, IR-8 Eval Infrastructure) have zero incident coverage; failure modes are heavily skewed toward prevention_failure (51/52); trust-integration split is dominated by "both" (46/52).
runs.name: AMCIS 2026 — Strategic AI Orientation Framework

datasets.description: 42 CIO competency statements derived from crosswalk analysis. Columns: "competency_id" = sequential ID (COMP-01..COMP-42), "req_id" = governance requirement ID (e.g. NIST-GV-1, EU-3, OWASP-6), "bundle" = capability bundle classification ("Trust Readiness" or "Integration Readiness"), "confidence" = evidence strength (high/medium/low), "competency_statement" = natural-language capability statement with [#XX] corpus citations, "bundle_reasoning" = why classified as Trust vs Integration, "applicable_controls" = semicolon-separated architecture controls, "evidence_summary" = supporting literature passages with source IDs.
datasets.name: step2_competency_statements.csv

datasets.description: JSON array of 42 crosswalk entries. Each entry maps one governance requirement to architecture controls with evidence. Keys: "req_id" = requirement ID, "applicable_controls" = array of matched architecture control names, "bundle" = Trust/Integration classification, "bundle_reasoning" = classification rationale, "confidence" = high/medium/low, "competency_statement" = derived capability statement, "evidence" = array of {control, source_id, passage, reasoning} objects linking each control to a specific literature passage.
datasets.name: step2_crosswalk_evidence.json

datasets.description: 42-row binary matrix. First 6 columns: "req_id" = governance requirement ID, "source" = normative framework (NIST AI RMF 1.0 / NIST GenAI Profile / EU AI Act / OWASP Top 10 LLM), "function" = framework function (GOVERN/MAP/MEASURE/MANAGE/GOVERNANCE/TRANSPARENCY/SECURITY), "requirement" = full requirement text, "bundle" = Trust Readiness or Integration Readiness, "competency_statement" = derived CIO competency. Remaining 18 columns are architecture controls (e.g. "RAG Architecture & Data Grounding", "Threat Modeling & Red-Teaming"); cells contain "X" if the requirement maps to that control, empty otherwise.
datasets.name: step2_crosswalk_matrix.csv

datasets.description: 16 rows, one per framework sub-competency. Columns: "sub_competency_id" = ID (TR-1..TR-8 for Trust Readiness, IR-1..IR-8 for Integration Readiness), "sub_competency_name" = label, "bundle" = Trust/Integration, "incident_count" = number of MITRE ATLAS incidents mapped, "coverage_status" = validated (3+) / partial (1-2) / uncovered (0), "incident_ids" = semicolon-separated case study IDs, "primary_harm_types" = top harm types with counts (e.g. "security(16); privacy(2)").
datasets.name: step3_coverage_map.csv

datasets.description: Markdown narrative version of the coverage map. Contains summary statistics, two tables (Trust Readiness and Integration Readiness sub-competency coverage), and a harm type distribution table across all 52 incidents.
datasets.name: step3_coverage_map.md

datasets.description: JSON array of 52 MITRE ATLAS case studies with incident coding. Key fields: "case_study_id" = ATLAS ID (AML.CS0000..AML.CS0051), "name"/"summary"/"incident_date" = incident metadata, "actor"/"target" = threat actor and target organisation, "tactics_used"/"techniques_used" = ATLAS taxonomy references, "harm_type" = primary harm category (security/privacy/reliability/autonomy_misuse/safety/bias_discrimination/intellectual_property/supply_chain), "failure_mode" = prevention_failure/detection_failure/response_failure, "trust_integration_split" = trust-dominant/integration-dominant/both, "llm_sub_competencies" = mapped sub-competency IDs, "llm_gap_description" = LLM-generated competency gap narrative, "chain_of_thought" = LLM reasoning trace.
datasets.name: step3_enrichments.json

runs.description:
This dataset consolidates three public secondary-data sources used in a
design-science / framework-synthesis study targeting AMCIS 2026.

Sources:
1. AIID – AI Incident Database (1,366 real-world AI failure incidents
   classified by harm domain, tangible harm, sector, autonomy level,
   AI technology, and technical failure type).
2. MITRE ATLAS – Adversarial Threat Landscape for AI Systems (84
   adversarial case studies coded with tactics, techniques, and
   mitigations; cross-mapped to McKinsey AI-scaling constraints C1–C8).
3. EO 13960 – U.S. Federal AI Use-Case Inventory (3,658 government AI
   deployments scored for governance readiness across two tiers: basic
   controls and deep governance safeguards including impact assessments,
   bias mitigation, and independent evaluation).

Analytical layers built on top of these three sources include:
- A crosswalk matrix linking 42 governance requirements from NIST AI RMF,
  EU AI Act, ISO 42001, and OWASP Top-10 LLM to 18 architecture controls.
- 16 sub-competencies in two bundles: Trust Readiness (TR-1…TR-8) and
  Integration Readiness (IR-1…IR-8).
- Incident-coding of ATLAS cases mapping tactics to competency gaps.
- Five testable propositions (P1–P5) with falsifiability criteria.

The CSV concatenates ALL tables (sparse — use the `source_table` column
to segment by data source). Supplementary .md and .json files provide
construct definitions, proposition narratives, and validation reports.

Known limitation: EO 13960 data skews toward U.S. federal agencies;
AIID coverage varies by year; ATLAS cases are curated (not exhaustive).
runs.name: AMCIS2026 – AI Orientation Trust-Integration Readiness

run_metadata.domain: Information Systems / AI Governance / Enterprise Architecture
run_metadata.intent: Investigate the relationship between governance readiness (trust readiness) and architecture controls (integration readiness) in AI deployments. Focus on: (1) patterns in governance gaps across the eo13960_scored data — especially why tier2 compliance is so low; (2) which ATLAS tactics and missing mitigations cluster together in incident_coding; (3) whether harm severity in AIID correlates with sector, autonomy level, or failure type; (4) cross-source patterns linking what CAN go wrong (ATLAS) with what HAS gone wrong (AIID) and what organizations ARE actually doing (EO13960). The source_table column distinguishes the 14 sub-tables.
